approach: Average velocity is the total displacement in the interval divided by the time, so write the displacement using the standard equation and divide by t.

steps.text: Write the displacement from 0 to time t using the standard equation of motion with constant acceleration a.
Average velocity over the interval is this displacement divided by the time taken.
Cancel t from each term to reach the simplest form.
steps.why_this_step: This also equals the mean of the initial and final velocities, (u + v)/2, since v = u + at.

common_mistakes.text: Taking the average velocity as u, the initial velocity, ignoring that the velocity keeps changing at rate a over the interval.
